text:
The Penguins are better than their record, and that may not matter. At 6-10-2 they have 14 points, but by the chances they've earned about 19, the biggest gap in the division. They take 52% of the five-on-five expected goals. What has sunk them is goaltending and finishing: Arturs Silovs is at .855 over his last five starts, and the team has scored a few goals fewer than its chances usually bring.

That gap is why the headlines are about who goes, not who comes. Evgeni Malkin's name is in trade-rumor pieces nearly every day, Erik Karlsson's is close behind, and all of it sits next to Sidney Crosby passing Marcel Dionne for sixth on the NHL's all-time scoring list on Saturday. It's a strange place for a franchise: celebrating history while the market wonders who'll be sold.

On the ice, the lines that are working are not the obvious ones. Connor Dewar, Blake Lizotte and Nick Robertson have outscored teams 4-1 with 54% of the chances, and Malkin's line with Tommy Novak and Egor Chinakhov is winning its minutes too. Our simulations give Pittsburgh a 17% playoff chance and project about 84 points, which is the bubble's far edge. If the goaltending turns, this team could climb fast. If it doesn't by the time the trade talk gets serious, the next month decides more than this season.
